    StartersPenguins' ice-cold sushi rollsSalmon and avocado rolls in nori, served with soyHow to make it300g sushi rice3 tbsp rice vinegar1 tbsp caster sugar4 nori sheets200g sashimi salmon1 avocado, sliced4 tbsp soy sauce2 tbsp pickled gingerCook the rice and season with vinegar and sugar. Cool.Spread over the nori, fill with salmon and avocado and roll tight with a mat.Slice with a wet knife.Serve with soy and pickled ginger. Smile and wave, boys.Island sweet potato fritters with mango salsaCrisp spiced sweet potato fritters with a mango, chilli and lime salsaHow to make it600g sweet potato, peeled and grated3 spring onions, sliced2 eggs75g plain flour1 tsp ground cumin80ml vegetable oil1 mango, diced1 long red chilli, finely chopped1 lime, juiced1 corianderSqueeze the grated sweet potato in a clean tea towel to dry it.Mix with the spring onions, eggs, flour, cumin and a good pinch of salt.Fry heaped spoonfuls in the oil over medium heat, flattened, 3 minutes a side until crisp and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.Mix the mango, chilli, lime juice and chopped coriander with a pinch of salt.Serve the fritters hot with the salsa on top.MainsAlex's steakPan seared rib eye, garlic butter, fries. Sweet, juicy steak.How to make it4 rib eye steaks2 tsp salt60g butter, softened2 garlic cloves, crushed2 tbsp chopped parsley1kg potatoes, cut into shoestrings2 L vegetable oil, for fryingSalt the steaks and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.Mash the butter with the garlic and parsley.Fry the shoestring potatoes in the vegetable oil until golden and crisp.Sear the steaks in a smoking cast iron pan, flipping every minute, and pull at 54°C.Rest for 8 minutes and top with the garlic butter.Madagascar coconut fish curryFish in coconut curry. Better than steak.How to make itAs written, serves 4Firm white fish simmered in a coconut, tomato and ginger curry with lime and chilli, served over rice with fresh coriander and toasted coconut.Soften 1 diced onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp grated ginger in oil.Add 2 tsp mild curry powder and 1 tsp turmeric and stir 1 minute.Add 2 diced tomatoes and 400ml coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes.Slip in 800g firm white fish such as barramundi in chunks and poach gently for 6 minutes.Finish with lime juice and salt.Serve over rice with coriander and toasted coconut flakes.SweetsKing Julien's caramel grilled pineappleGrilled pineapple wedges in brown sugar caramel butterHow to make it1 pineapple, cut into long wedges60g butter80g brown sugar1 lime, juiced1 pinch salt1 tub coconut ice cream50g coconut flakes, toastedGrill the pineapple on a hot pan for 3 minutes a side until charred.Melt the butter with the sugar, bubble for 2 minutes, then stir in the lime juice and salt.Toss the pineapple in the caramel.Serve warm with scoops of coconut ice cream and toasted coconut flakes.Marty's birthday zebra browniesZebra-striped chocolate brownies. Don't abuse the wish.How to make it150g dark chocolate120g butter250g caster sugar3 eggs80g plain flour200g cream cheeseMelt the chocolate with the butter, whisk in most of the sugar and two eggs and fold in the flour.Beat the cream cheese with the rest of the sugar and the last egg.Spread the brownie in a tin and swirl the cheesecake through in stripes.Bake at 170°C for 30 minutes.DrinksKing Julien's mango passionfruit punchMango, pineapple, passionfruit and lime, for the New York giantsHow to make it600ml mango nectar300ml pineapple juice4 passionfruits, pulp2 limes, juiced, plus wedges1 mango, diced600ml chilled lemonade3 cups crushed iceIn a large jug stir the nectar, pineapple juice, passionfruit pulp and lime juice.Add diced mango and plenty of crushed ice.Top with lemonade just before serving and pour into tall glasses with a lime wedge.
